Dashlane review: digital legacy verdict

Verdict: Not recommended for legacy access. Dashlane removed its Emergency Contact feature and now suggests sharing an exported vault file with a trusted person.

Best for: People who use Dashlane for day-to-day passwords and plan legacy access some other way.

Pricing: Check current pricing.

Official site / docs ↗

Pros

  • Polished, easy-to-use apps
  • Account Recovery Key helps you regain access if you forget your master password

Cons

  • No emergency contact or dead-man's-switch feature
  • The export-and-share workaround goes stale as passwords change
  • The recovery key is for the account owner, not for heirs

FAQ

What is Dashlane best for?

People who use Dashlane for day-to-day passwords and plan legacy access some other way.

Bitwarden

The best-value password manager with real emergency access: trusted contacts can request View or Takeover access after a wait time you set.

Vaults & password managers

1Password

Excellent password manager, but it has no automatic emergency-access feature. Legacy planning relies on the Emergency Kit and family account recovery.

Vaults & password managers

Keeper

A solid choice with built-in Emergency Access: name trusted contacts who can request your vault after a wait period.
